newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Labour Board sees 6.5 pct unemployed 1998.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Labour Board sees 6.5 pct unemployed 1998.

text.p: Sweden's Labour Market Board (AMS) expected unemployment to fall to 6.5 percent in 1998 from an expected level of 7.1 percent this year, Swedish news agency TT said on Tuesday.
In addition, the board expects an average of 5.5 percent of the work force to be placed in government work schemes during both years.
These forecasts were to be included in an AMS report on unemployment that will be presented to the minority Social Democratic government this week.
AMS saw employment rising by 40,000 people in 1998 compared with 1997, while it expected the work force to increase by 15,000 people.
The decrease in unemployment follows an expected increase in demand, in turn fuelled by stronger construction trends and higher real wages, TT said.

But the board's forecast is gloomier than the government's outlook in its September 1996 budget proposal, which targeted unemployment of 6.1 percent in 1998 with another five percent of the work force in government work schemes.
The difference between the board's and the government's forecasts corresponds to 40,000 people, TT said.
The board has not taken into account the extra 10 billion crowns that the government has promised to spend on health care, elderly care, child care and schools in 1998.
In January this year, unemployment stood at 8.8 percent.
Prime Minister Goran Persson has promised to halve unemployment but the general election in September 1998.
